source.quote: Greetings travelers and welcome back to Goldbound, the challenge series where our rogue Goldilock is exploring the World of Warcraft by unlocking one zone at a time and in each new zone exploring and discovering gold farms until we earn enough gold to buy a WoW token. And last episode, we left off just short of the WoW token and farming in our most recently unlocked zone, Dust Wallow Marsh. But we already found some really solid farms here. So, I figure we should just lock in and do the Dust Wall Gauntlet until the token is earned. Current status is 212,000 gold out of 260,000 gold for the token. So, let's check the mailbox. As you can see here, I did send over all the gold and the loot from my alts that sell Transmog.

source.quote: Of course, there's Alderman, home to not one, but two dungeons, actually. Then, we have the dragon's mouth. This is a scar from Deathwing, but actually a little bit of a gold mine. Plus, there's fuse light, a goblin stronghold. Time is money, friend. New carath. and not to mention quite a few different types of welps, beasts, and rares hanging around the zone. Let's just say there's a lot to explore, but what better way to get started on the zone than by getting in a few runs of Alderman, the new zone dungeon. Now, Alderman is an interesting dungeon and one that I have been looking forward to unlocking in this challenge for quite some time because at its core, it's basically a transmog lottery. Throughout the whole dungeon, there's a ton of dungeon zone BOE drops. On top of that, there's quite a few green BOE sets, but the green BOE sets, while not terrible, aren't worth a crazy amount. For example, take the Huntsman set. These items can drop throughout the dungeon, and they're generally sold for between 1 to 2,000 gold. So, while not particularly valuable, I'll still keep them to build out the Transmog auction house. What we would most definitely like to see, though, is one of the Alderman super drops. This is the same angle as the Vashir pickpocketing or the sunken temple runs with some of the rare BOE drops. But in Alderman, the value of these items can range from 500,000 gold to near gold cap depending on the pull.

source.cleaned_file: goldbound/034 - I Rolled A Zone Where Drops Are Worth MILLIONS - Goldbound Ep.33.en-orig.txt
source.quote: Of course, these items are super rare, and quite honestly, even after a thousand runs of this dungeon, they still could not drop. But let's talk about them. First up, and probably one of the most well-known drops here, Papal Fez. This hat has some good value, not only because of its low drop chance, but also the rarity of its appearance. It's one of the only fez looking hats in the game. There's reports of this one going for gold cap in the past, but based on recent trade skill master data, the average price is probably closer to 2.3 mil with recent sales more consistently in the 1.2 million gold range. Still a crazy good item. Then we have the Pendulum of Doom. Arguably one of the best super items to get in Alderman today. This item in particular used to be a twink item back in the day, but now its value is pretty much solely from its unique appearance and its rarity with market values over 3.3 million gold. Not to mention, region average sales well over 1 million. But to be honest, a lot of these items are so rare that they tend to sell so infrequently and with quite a few sales going off market playerto-player through forums and just trade windows that it's a bit hard to nail down a true price. On top of the big two there though, we have some more.

source.cleaned_file: goldbound/034 - I Rolled A Zone Where Drops Are Worth MILLIONS - Goldbound Ep.33.en-orig.txt
source.quote: The likes of the Dig Master 5000, which is so rare that it has very little recent auction house data except for a recent listing at 8 million gold. But realistically, this thing is worth anywhere from 500k to gold cap, depending on the buyer and how bad they want it. Then, similar to the dig master is the miner's hat of the deep. This one does have a pretty cool appearance and honestly, one that would definitely fit the goldy gold farming vibe, but again, very little sale data on this one, but an average list price of about 5 million gold. These values are actually insane. But there's more, because we have the Spalders of Lost Age and the Jackhammer still. Both of these are well into the class of super items and have insane market values to match, but likewise low sale data. But with all that hype with a millions of gold and potential gold cap for sales, the chance of getting any of these items is insanely low from Alderman, which really shows in the listing data. Even though hundreds of players every single day are farming this dungeon, the market movement and how often they even appear on the auction house is insanely low. But those are just the rarest of the unique blue boe from Alderman. And there's an even wider table of less rare blue boes, which they're a little less rare and not classed as super items, but can still pull some massive sales between 20k and 500k. I would say the best of these rare non-super items is probably the Jins Su sword. This is one of those classic assassin appearances sword that sheath's on the back, which now that transmog allows you to sheath any weapon on the back, the value might get hit a little bit, but recent values on this are right around 500,000 gold just for the sword, which is crazy because the best of the low value items in this dungeon is basically the cream of the crop in any other dungeon in the game. But we know what we want in Alderman. The real question now is how are we going to farm it? Because Alderman is quite a bit of a maze. There's a few different meta routes you can do, but as I farm this while we're locked into the Badlands, I'm going to optimize a route for Goldie cuz I think there's a few angles. It's definitely big enough that if we wanted to, we could plan a small route within the dungeon to optimize it to be 6 minutes per run and 10 runs per hour. Or we could just optimize a full clear route, which would take 12 to 15 minutes per run, and we'd get 3 to 5 runs per hour. I'll see which one I prefer, but in general here, the more mobs in Alderman, the better. The super drops are zone drops across the whole dungeon and can technically drop from every single mob including bosses. And on top of that, there's tons of chests in the dungeon, like this one beside the scorpion dens, which is also accompanied by an enchanting trainer. If we didn't already have enchanting from Elwin and Dustallow, this would have been quite the unlock. Then we have the chest here in between a few bosses and then another chest after the final boss. And since Goldie is a rogue, I can just pick these chests if they're locked, which is about 50% of the time. But if you're wanting to run this on a druid or an alternative class, you definitely can. But just make sure to bring inscription lockpicking scrolls or some other lockpicking item so you can get all the drops because you do not want to miss out on the chests.

source.quote: Well, the full set except for the chest piece of course. I think Goldie is just cursed to have no chest. But this does pair pretty well with an Alderman and just general badland set. And with the green vibe, I think I know just the weapons to go with it. Oh yeah, new set. And I'm liking it. Maybe the next chest piece that we'll equip will be the night slayer chest. Maybe. Until then though, we really got to get some more gold going. We do have a good chunk of raw gold going from Alderman. About 9.5k, which speaking of raw gold, I'll definitely go back to check out the dragonfly version of Alderman, the legacy of tier, which I think will also be a raw gold angle. But since we already have raw gold and some chances at super items, I think what we need now is a reliable, steady money maker. Are you thinking what I'm thinking? It's time for dual gathering. Let's go. So, I went ahead here and took the time to level up herbalism to about 175, which should be plenty to get the full rates of herbs here. And I already have level 200 mining from Dustallow Marsh. So, we should be good on that front. At first glance, it seems like Badlands will be pretty solid dual gathering rates to be honest. It's a pretty open map and while not a circle, there's at least no trees to get in the way. Plus, from a mining perspective, it has a rather valuable resource, myithil ore. Generally speaking, in these oldw world zones, if we can find highdensity thorium or myithil ore, it should mean pretty decent gold per hour. And at first glance, there's a ton of it. On top of that, there's also a few spawns of silver ore, gold ore, and true silver ore. So, all around pretty darn good.

source.cleaned_file: goldbound/034 - I Rolled A Zone Where Drops Are Worth MILLIONS - Goldbound Ep.33.en-orig.txt
source.quote: And as far as herbalism goes, we have a bit of a wider variety. So, we're getting Fire Bloom, which comes in around eight gold each. Golden Sands Sam, which is pretty cheap and about two or three gold each. Sungrass at about five gold. But then the big one, Dragon's Teeth, over 20 gold each. Dragon's Teeth is an interesting one, though, because it only spawns in the middle of the zone around the dragon's mouth and the massive scar that Deathwing left behind. But, it does spawn pretty readily in that small area, so it's definitely worth flying through and picking up. So, with that in mind, my route is looking something like this. Looping around the whole zone, getting every herb and ore we see, and then popping into the middle of the zone for a few more mining nodes, but also primarily the dragon's teeth. And the results from an hour of farming. Well, we got 411 Myithil ore as well as 462 solid stone alongside a few gold and a few silver ore. So, a pretty respectable mining rate. Then we got 63 fire bloom, 54 golden sandsom, 84 dragon's teeth, and 129 sungrass. And when we add up the market values, it comes out to around 6,500 gold per hour. And honestly, pretty respectable. But after this first hour with the values of dragon teeth and myithal ore, I really think we can improve this. So I'm actually going to run it back for another hour. And instead of stopping for all the herbs, I'm only going to get Myithrilore around the perimeter of the zone, doing loops, and then once every lap, pop into the center to the dragon scar to snag all of the dragon's teeth. I think in theory, this should optimize the value per node, and we won't waste time dismounting for sungrass and sandsome because on the first run, we definitely weren't limited by spawn rates. It was just how fast we could grab them. And with this, the results, oh, it's an improvement. The myithal ore per hour went up to 652.

source.quote: I don't want to sell them just yet at market value because I think we might be able to process them into some increased profits, but I mean, I can't complain. We have a pretty darn good dual gathering route here in Badlands right off the bat. So, with that in the back pocket, onto the next farm. And this one is up in the ruins of Cargath because just look at this. This place is crawling with Mandre's broodlings. Welps. And these welps are literally all over the place. But to be fair, the hills are also pretty aggressive, so it can be kind of hard to run around and kill them. To test out killing speed, I might try farming these guys both in outlaw spec, where I can use my grappling hook to jump up clips and around the hills, but then also try it out in subtlety spec where I can use shrew and storm and maybe AoE them down a little bit. But since we just leveled up our dual gathering and it seems to be pretty good per hour, I don't actually have skinning for this. And these guys would skin into thick and rugged leather, but I think not having skinning might be okay because we're actually farming these welps for the dark welping. This is the same welp that drops in the searing gorge wetlands and dustall marsh. And while there's a ton of welps for us to kill here, it does have quite a low drop rate of 1 in, 1250. So the more kills per hour that we can tag, the better our chances of ending up with a wealth will be. So, from a purely welling perspective, if we stop the skin each mob, it would definitely slow down the total kills.

source.file: 034 - I Rolled A Zone Where Drops Are Worth MILLIONS - Goldbound Ep.33.en-orig.vtt
source.cleaned_file: goldbound/034 - I Rolled A Zone Where Drops Are Worth MILLIONS - Goldbound Ep.33.en-orig.txt
source.quote: Our expected value here comes out to about 10,150 gold per hour. But, of course, we still have to get the welp and sell the welp. But that's Outlaw. What about subtlety spec? Because in sub, we have a few movement speed abilities as well, but the main thing here is shuriken storm where you can maybe kill a couple mobs at once. But after testing this out, sub actually ends up being about 828 kills per hour and about 20% fewer than outlaw. All in all, I think the loss of base movement speed plus in this terrain missing out on grappling hooks is massive. As for the dark welping though, I still haven't sold the one I got in wetlands. So I'll just do an hour or so more here to see if I can snag one real quick before moving on to some other farms. But this would definitely be a good spot to restock if we ever need to. Boom. And there we go. Only about 900 kills into the session as well. Dark welping obtained. I'll get this listed and increase our total dark welp stock to two, which we also technically got one back in the day in Searing Gorge and sold it for about 12,000 gold. So, our third dark welping drop of the character. Hopefully, another sale coming soon. So, we have another high value item on the table, but I actually know of a spot that there might be a whole new angle. A raw gold farm. So far on the character within our zone restrictions, our best raw gold farms are generally raid clears and not something we can just run on repeat. But here, well, we have the Alderman legacy of tier, the dragon flight version of Alderman. Now, this does raise a few interesting aspects. First, we don't actually one-shot the mobs in here. And second, potentially gear upgrades to hopefully get some item level. And thirdly, of course, raw gold because this is a higher level expansion dungeon. So, not only does the gear bender for much more, but the actual mobs drop a ton of raw gold. Not to mention, if we run skinning here, we actually gain the dragon isles skinning skill and can get some Dragon Aisle skins, like these adamant scales. But this isn't the first time we've had access to adamant scales. We kind of looked into this whole angle on Stranglethorn veil when we had access to the Booty Bay Crocs and these skins. And unfortunately, the skins aren't worth too much and we can't actually process them further because we don't have access to Dragon Isles profession workbenches or Dragon A's profession trainers yet. But for us here, it does give us a little bit of extra and consistent gold. But moving on to the gear, this one is also an interesting angle because the dungeon doesn't just have normal difficulty, but heroic and mythic difficulty as well. And in normal, the gear we're getting is item level 73. And for reference, the Huntsman set that we got from Old Elderman, also all the epics from Molten Core are actually item level 74 and pretty much the exact same stats. So I think the stat squishes and the item level squishes over the years, not to mention the different phases you can be in Chromy time. Pretty much everything for us is the same item level. I think at least until we get close to current content. Even doing this dungeon on heroic gives us the same gear, the same item level, and it vendors for the same amount. The only technical upgrade is on mythic difficulty, which does grant item level 786, which ends up being a pretty marginal upgrade and on most pieces only ends up being about one extra stamina.

source.quote: So maybe not a gearing angle. But the raw gold, oh yeah, there's raw gold. So after testing this one for a while, I found that the best way to spam this dungeon for raw gold is to pretty much just pull everything up to the bosses and then wait for all the mobs to collect, kill them down, loot, and repeat on to the next boss. The dwarves we're exploring here with you have a few sections of RP dialogue. So, it's best to get that started while we're killing down the mobs. And because of that, even with this optimized route, I could only get the full clear down to about 7 minutes with the reset. So, it works out to about nine runs per hour. But those nine runs are pulling in some consistent gold. So, here's the math. From trade goods, orbs, cloth, and dragon scales, all of which are dragon isles level, we get about 650 gold or about 72 gold per run. However, from raw currency looted and total gold looted, we get about 4500 gold per hour or 500 per run. That's actually quite solid and makes it by far our best raw gold farm so far because the gold looted and vendor gold, it just goes straight into the bags. No auction house, no market, no waiting for sales, and no auction house fees, just instant gold. This could definitely come in handy if we ever need an instant influx of gold. Adding on the trade goods though, we're looking at about 5,150 gold per hour, making it a really solid farm, at least for other zones, but a little behind pace in the Badlands where we have quite a few other good options.

source.quote: But all of this is looking pretty good. So, let's get it all looted up and see where we sit. Okay. Okay. So, up to about 60,000 gold on Goldie, but we do have a few more transmog alts to check. First up, the backlog alt, and it looks like we're doing pretty good, particularly on Dark Moon Fair drops. I haven't gone back to get more Moonfang pelts since we were in the zone for the challenge. And these backlog ones are selling like crazy all of a sudden. It's currently the start of the Dark Moon Fair, so I guess people are really wanting to get the monthly Moon Fang quest done right away. On top of that, we even have a lock banan bare skin rug for 7,000 gold and a few odds and ends of older transmogs. Looting it all up though and it's about 43.5,000 gold. Pretty solid. How about the Badlands only transmog tune? We've spent quite a bit of time in Alderman, so I'm hoping a few of our lowerpriced blues or greens have sold. Okay, not too great. Only about 1.3k, which I'll probably just leave on the alt to cover posting fees. And that puts us up to about6,000 gold total out of around 260k for the token. And we already have quite a few good farms to unlock here. But there are definitely more to discover, and we can definitely spend some more time on the favorite ones. And while hitting the gas in the farms and pushing for that next WoW token, what better spot to hang out than Fuse Light by the sea? a nice goblin ocean town which has a few forges and uh some of the better vendor finds in the zone. Take Buck Slappy here. He has some pretty solided limited supply engineering recipes. But this isn't all we have here at Fuse Lake by the Sea because we also have the only fishable water in the whole zone at least so far that I've been able to find. And since the Dark Moon Fair is in town, I am popping down here every hour or so to use my Dark Moon Fair fishing hat to get my one to two Dark Moon fire water. But doing that has got me wondering, how good is the ocean fishing gold per hour here? Because as it turns out, there are a few fish that we can catch. The likes of fire fin snappers, stonecale eels, and summer bass. But the ones we really care about, well, the first one is the raw glossy mightfish. Not to be confused with its counterpart, the large raw mightfish. That one can sell for upwards of 500 gold. Unfortunately, the raw and glossy version is only worth about 10 gold each. Not ideal, but the raw spotted yellowtails that we pull in quite consistently, might I add, are actually worth 20 to 30 gold each with current prices up to 32 gold at the moment. So, these guys are definitely the angle here. And the other fish aren't worthless. They are worth about 1 to 10 gold each. And all in all, it ends up being a relatively decent little fishing farm. After logging a few casts here and testing it out, at least with current market values, I'm consistently reeling in about 4,500 gold per hour here. and actually a sneaky decent little fishing farm. If this one had large rawite fish, it would have actually been insane. But really, with the farms that we have access to right now, I do want to spend some time juicing the gold on dual gathering, as well as some scorpion alderman runs. At the moment, the experience I'm getting on Goldie from the herbs and ore nodes is pretty much all that's progressing us towards the next level. But with over 3 days played on level 83, I think one of these next dragon's teeth is going to ding us to 84. There it is. Ding. Level 84. These come pretty few and far between now on Goldie, so it's always nice to see. And we got here from farming quite a few of these things on top of several thousand myithal ore, which I'm mostly smelting into bars now.
